title: NeuroEdge Gated Tool Profile — tool result v1
description: What a caller (an LLM, an MCP client) is told back for one tool call: the `structuredContent` of the MCP result and the `outputSchema` of every tool. `status` decides: ALLOW, BLOCK or REJECTED. `reason` is an explanation only, never a reason to branch toward ALLOW; a `reason` the reader does not know, under BLOCK, is still a BLOCK (fail-closed). Result objects are open: a reader ignores keys it does not know. Pin `properties.tool` to a tool's name with a `const` when embedding this as that tool's `outputSchema` (the runtime also drops `$id` and `$schema` there).

tool.description: Name of the tool the call named.

status.description: ALLOW: the gate admitted the call and the action ran. BLOCK: the gate refused it. REJECTED: the call never reached a gate (unknown tool, or arguments that do not match the tool's inputSchema). Closed set: a new status is a v2.

gate.description: URI of the gate that decided. Present under BLOCK.

reason.description: Why the gate blocked, in words a log reader can use. Open string; the values known today are listed in `x-neuroedge-known`. Never branch toward ALLOW on it.

failed_criterion.description: Name of the criterion that failed, when one did.

on_block.description: What the gate did about the block (the `on_block.action` of gate.v1.json). Present under BLOCK. Closed set, equal to gate.v1.json.

message.description: Wording the gate gives for the block.

escalated_to.description: Who the request was escalated to, under `on_block: escalate`.

problems.description: What is wrong with the call. Present, and non-empty, under REJECTED.

fallback.description: Under `on_block: degrade`: the fallback action that ran through its own gate, told back in the same shape.

confirmation.description: Under `on_block: ask`: a person must answer on the device; the caller cannot.
